sampling_model.design: Randomized finite-arm instrument with \(\lambda_z=P(Z=z)>0\) for every population arm, with inference conditional on the realized positive arm counts \((n_z:z\in\mathcal Z)\).
sampling_model.units: Independent units from a law in \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal T,\mathcal C}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The realized exposure lies in \(\mathcal X=\mathcal T\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal C\); target levels obey exclusion and off-target levels have saturated arm-specific responses.
sampling_model.overlap: Population positivity \(\lambda_z>0\) defines every conditional arm law \(p_z\) and skeleton law \(s_z\). The separate realized-sample condition \(n_z\ge1\) is required for finite-sample calibration; positive limiting arm proportions and an interior skeleton are used solely for the regular-face lower bound.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated: conditional on fixed finite arm counts, off-target allocations \(\eta_z\) factor variation-independently, induce finite-fiber kernels \(K_\eta(\nu\mid\sigma)\), and are removed before KL calibration.

body.tldr: Only selected levels of a finely recorded exposure may define meaningful interventions. Under positive-probability random assignment and exclusion restricted to those levels, the saturated target-only model has an exact quotient: the sharp law of the target potential-outcome vector is the image of a reduced response simplex that keeps target outcome cells and one off-target mass per arm. A boundary-safe right inverse removes the number and labels of off-target categories. Conditional on fixed finite arm counts, a rule-specific convexity inequality yields exact equality of the full and skeleton nuisance-minimax values without asserting pointwise risk domination, and a reduced method-of-types confidence region has calibration independent of \( |\mathcal C| \). The exact kink frontier is left as an open question.

project_justification.gap: Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander report the attested low-cardinality target-contrast bound coincidences. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson provide attested categorical potential-outcome notation. These results motivate, but under the presently attested excerpts do not establish a formal inclusion or equivalence with, the saturated target-only model studied here.
project_justification.niche: The model has common potential outcomes only on \(\mathcal T\), saturated \(R_{c,z}\) on \(\mathcal C\), and the complete law of \(Y_{\mathcal T}\) as the target. Its comparator positioning is motivation-only under the available attestations.
project_justification.fill: The quotient and its boundary-safe right inverse give sharp identification for arbitrary finite cardinalities. Internally defined structural and arm-invariant response classes admit explicit algebraic comparisons, without attribution to a published model. In the conditional product experiment, a rule-specific convexity reduction and nuisance-invariant lift give equality of nuisance-minimax values without pointwise risk domination; reduced KL projection gives kink-robust finite-sample coverage; and polyhedral stability converts its radius to a target-set excess bound.

body.related_work: Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander \cite{GabrielSachsSjolander2025} report the attested low-cardinality target-contrast bound coincidences described in Results 1 and 3. Those results motivate the target-only quotient problem; no published-class inclusion or response-law equivalence is claimed from the present attestation. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson \cite{SongGuoChanRichardson2024} introduce categorical outcome, treatment, and instrument variables, potential outcomes \(Y(x,z)\), and the notation \(Y(x):=Y(x,Z)\); this is categorical potential-outcome motivation only under the attested excerpt. The common-response versus saturated comparison below is an internal algebraic result, not an identification with their published model. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjölander, and Gabriel \cite{SachsJonzonSjolanderGabriel2023} provide response-function incidence machinery; Guo and Richardson \cite{GuoRichardson2021} provide an alphabet-generic relative-entropy concentration tool. Blackwell \cite{Blackwell1953} supplies the experiment-comparison template, while the unknown allocation kernel necessitates nuisance-minimax rather than pointwise comparison. Hoffman \cite{Hoffman1952} and Li \cite{Li1993} supply generic polyhedral error-bound tools. Levis et al. \cite{LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025} and Gafarov \cite{Gafarov2025} locate the active-facet inference problem but do not settle the target-specific kink frontier. Boushehrian et al. \cite{BoushehrianBadriAkbariKiyavash2026} show why exponential dependence on substantive support can remain after irrelevant off-target cardinality is removed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The structural-form transfer and arm-invariant response-type bijection are internally defined algebraic constructions and are not attributed to the published Gabriel or Song model classes. The present attestations do not support a published-model inclusion or equivalence claim. The method-of-types radius is deliberately elementary and may be larger than the polynomial Chernoff calibration of Guo and Richardson; the contribution is the target-specific quotient that removes \( |\mathcal C| \), not a new multinomial tail inequality. The nuisance-minimax comparison is confined to the finite count experiment conditional on fixed arm counts and is not a pointwise domination statement. The exact smallest Hoffman constant and the nonregular kink law are not presupposed, and no additional rate theorem is introduced here.
body.honest_scope: The equality of full and reduced identified images is sharp and includes an explicit boundary-safe right inverse for the separately defined saturated target-only model. The available Gabriel and Song attestations are used only for the narrow statements recorded on their cited nodes; no published-class inclusion, response-law equivalence, or strict extension is claimed. The structural-form and arm-invariant bijection lemmas are internally defined algebraic constructions. The finite-count nuisance-minimax theorem, finite-sample whole-set coverage, finite Hoffman certificate, and regular-face lower bound remain separate theorem obligations. The condition \(\lambda_z>0\) only makes population conditional arm laws well defined, whereas \(n_z\ge1\) concerns the realized conditional experiment. The exact face-by-face minimax law and an adaptive attaining procedure at dual ties remain the open kink question. When \(\mathcal C=\varnothing\), \(m=2\), and \(|\mathcal T|=2\), the construction reduces to the classical Balke--Pearl response-type program.
